source: CLAUDE.md §3.4(c) and §3.4(e); CONTRACTS.md §1.4. Seriousness criterion for hospitalization from ICH E2A (1994) §II.B.
rationale: Red flags are conditions that bypass composite grading and set a floor on the escalation tier so that an urgent situation is never under-triaged by the grade crosswalk alone. They are evaluated after grading and before vitals. A 'severe item' is defined once here so every rule means the same thing: for items that ask severity, severity >= 3 (Severe or Very severe); for items that do not ask severity, a composite of 3. Conditions are declarative so the rule and its threshold are visible as data; the engine evaluates them without any clinical number in code.

severe_item_definition.note: severity >= 3 means the participant chose Severe or Very severe.

rules.description: Severe or very severe shortness of breath
Fever or chills present together with at least one severe item
Participant reports a hospital admission or emergency-room visit since the last visit
rules.effect: tier floor = 3 (Urgent); seriousness suspected; SAE clock starts

rules.description: Free-text comment present together with at least one severe item
rules.effect: tier floor = 2 (Nurse call today); flag for human read; text is never parsed
